chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu al-Hasan al-Ahmasi said:

Sa'id ibn Yasar asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person in ihram who has a wound, blister, or boil, and he said: 'Place on it the banafsjah (violet/colocynth) or the shiraj (cucumber) and similar things that do not have a sweet scent.'

key_terms.الْبَنَفْسَجَ: A type of medicinal plant (violet or colocynth)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What can a person in ihram apply to a wound or boil if it has no sweet scent?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between medicinal application and the prohibition of scent (*rih tayyibah*) for the *muhrim*. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that natural plant essences are permissible if their scent is not overpowering or added as a distinct perfume, thereby balancing ritual purity with practical medical needs during the sacred state.
